NetworkDefinitionModel.description:
One virtual network: its address space, subnets and optional peerings. Each network is its own cloud resource, so its configuration, custom values and tags are set here; one document can hold several networks.

Rules:
- Subnet names must be unique within the network.
- Peering names must be unique within the network, and a network cannot peer with itself.
- Subnets must not overlap each other and must fit inside the network's address space. This is only checked when all the CIDRs involved are literals rather than tokens.

name.description: Unique network name within the spec

address_space.description: One or more CIDRs for this network's address space (literal or '${var:KEY}'/'${secret:KEY}'/'${feature:KEY}' Value bindings)

subnets.description: At least one subnet required per network

peerings.description: Optional peering references to other networks

configuration.description: Free-form provisioner settings for this network, passed to Terraform as `strata.networks.<name>.networks.<network>.configuration`. Strata does not validate them.

custom.description: Free-form values for your own scripts and Terraform code, passed to Terraform as `strata.networks.<name>.networks.<network>.custom`. Strata does not interpret them.

default_tags.description: Baseline cloud tags for this network (for example `cost-center`, `environment`, `owner`), passed to Terraform as `strata.networks.<name>.networks.<network>.default_tags`. Not the same as `meta.tags`, which is a free-form list for documentation. Strata does not limit the number of tags, so stay within your cloud provider's limit.

custom_tags.description: Additional cloud tags on top of `default_tags`, for one-off needs.

NetworkMetaModel.description: Network metadata including name, annotations, labels, and tags.

name.description: Unique name for the network resource

tags.description: Optional list of tags for the network resource

NetworkSpecModel.description:
The networks declared by this document.

Rules:
- Network names must be unique within the document.
- Every peering `target` must name a network in the same document.
- Peered networks must not have overlapping address spaces. This is only checked for literal CIDRs.

networks.description:
List of network definitions (at least one required)

Rules:
- Subnet names must be unique within the network.
- Peering names must be unique within the network, and a network cannot peer with itself.
- Subnets must not overlap each other and must fit inside the network's address space. This is only checked when all the CIDRs involved are literals rather than tokens.

PeeringReferenceModel.description: Lightweight peering reference — name + target network only.

name.description: Unique peering name within the network

target.description: Name of the target network (must exist in same spec)

SubnetModel.description: A subnet of a network: a `name` and a `cidr`, either a literal CIDR such as `10.0.1.0/24` or a string with value tokens such as `${var:KEY}`.

name.description: Unique subnet name within the network

cidr.description: Literal CIDR (e.g. '10.0.1.0/24'), or a string containing '${var:KEY}'/'${secret:KEY}'/'${feature:KEY}' tokens.

configuration.description: Free-form provisioner settings for this subnet (for example delegations, service endpoints or a security group association), passed to Terraform as `strata.networks.<name>.networks.<network>.subnets.<subnet>.configuration`. Strata does not validate them.

custom.description: Free-form values for your own scripts and Terraform code, passed to Terraform as `strata.networks.<name>.networks.<network>.subnets.<subnet>.custom`. Strata does not interpret them.

description: Virtual networks with their address spaces, subnets and peerings. A workspace uses it by listing the document in `networks`, and a workspace resource can be placed on one of its subnets.

spec.description:
Network specification (network definitions)

Rules:
- Network names must be unique within the document.
- Every peering `target` must name a network in the same document.
- Peered networks must not have overlapping address spaces. This is only checked for literal CIDRs.
